bearings.paper_claim: The second dimension now adds less than 1 percent improvement in classification over the first in both chambers (p.7). Party overlap, measured as the share of a party's members closer to the opposing party's mean than to their own, is under 1.5 percent in both chambers for the past 5 Congresses, with none in the past 3 Senates (p.15). The paper does not discuss final-passage votes specifically; the inference that a single final-passage vote mostly records party position is the analyst's, not the paper's.
bearings.paper_location: Sec. 3 p.7-8; Sec. 5 p.15 (Fig 9 not in extracted text)
bearings.system_side: vote_corroboration() (Path V) marks a category as corroborated when vote_category_lean.json shows lean >= 0.5 with n >= 1 for the member; it does not condition on party or ideal point. Verifier re-ran the same function on 2026-10-09 (window = current vote_category_lean.json; denominators = moneyball_core.party() roster counts, D 259, R 271, I 3 excluded) and got identical shares: CFPB D 4/259 (2%) vs R 179/271 (66%); Technology & Emerging D 18 (7%) vs R 263 (97%); Examination & Supervision D 106 (41%) vs R 261 (96%); CU Capital Requirements D 9 (3%) vs R 149 (55%); Charter Modernization D 215 (83%) vs R 70 (26%); NCUA Budget & Insurance D 145 (56%) vs R 51 (19%). Not every category sorts by party: Mortgage & Housing D 78% vs R 74%, Fraud Prevention 63% vs 68%, Defense CU Issues 57% vs 58%. Correct category names are 'CU Capital Requirements' and 'NCUA Budget & Insurance'.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Paper evidence ends at the 105th Congress (1998). The party split is a re-run of the same function, not an independent second method, so it stays UNVERIFIED under DE-062 and is quoted stratified by party only. The qualification applies to the party-sorted categories, not to Mortgage & Housing, Fraud Prevention or Defense CU Issues.

The authors let legislators serving as few as 3 Congresses get linear terms, admitting random walkers will appear linear, a bias deliberately in favour of the polynomial models.

bearings.paper_claim: Party overlap is under 1.5 percent in both chambers for the past 5 Congresses (p.15). The paper states, citing McCarty, Poole and Rosenthal (1999) rather than presenting evidence, that party per se does not account for much roll-call voting over and above the spatial model (p.17).

bearings.transfer_conditions: With near-zero overlap, dim1 and party are nearly collinear; the informative test is within-party. A pooled coefficient carries the UNSTRATIFIED label.

bearings.paper_claim: Parties in Congress are, for the most part, spatially adjacent ideological coalitions (p.17, citing Krehbiel 1993), and party overlap is near zero (p.15). The paper does not discuss partitions of networks or cutting-line members.
bearings.system_side: signed_coalitions.py is a diagnostic Aref-Neal frustration partition of the signed mention layer (member_references.json), with a party-recovery check and cross-party hidden-coalition candidates; nothing in the chain consumes it.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Benchmark only: checking hidden-coalition candidates against |dim1| would show whether the mention layer adds information beyond roll-call ideology. Does not reinstate DW-NOMINATE vote edges, which Paul rejected (brain cosponsor-and-sector-networks topic, line 93).
bearings.verifier_note: Code docstring confirmed. The paper_claim's two-group partition and cutting-line statements were analyst inference and are removed.

bearings.paper_claim: The second dimension now adds less than 1 percent improvement over the first dimension in both chambers.
bearings.system_side: blended_engine_priority adds PRIORITY_ORIENTATION_ALPHA (0.15 flip, 0.25 coalition) times engine_orientation, a fixed-IMP-weighted mean of the member's category stance scores excluding the current topic.
bearings.transfer_conditions: engine_orientation reads category_stance scores, not votes. The Path V vote shares (UNVERIFIED) show opposite party direction across some categories (CFPB, Technology, Exam, CU Capital Requirements lean R; Charter, NCUA Budget & Insurance lean D) and none in others. If stance scores share that pattern, leave-one-out borrowing could import party sign; that has not been checked on the stance scores. Alpha is small.
bearings.verifier_note: Code confirmed. The analyst's 'CU orientation is not the NOMINATE dimension' was drawn from vote data while the engine uses stance scores; reworded as conditional.

related.why: Aref and Neal partition signed House co-sponsorship networks (1981-2017) and find the optimal 2-partition and especially the 3-partition leave fewer frustrated edges than the party partition, with a fluid third coalition. NOMINATE dim1 is a natural benchmark for whether those members are more than near-center moderates.
Earlier optimal signed partition of House and Senate co-sponsorship networks (sessions 96-114); its coalitions can be checked against DW-NOMINATE ideal points.
Bonica estimates candidate and contributor ideal points from contribution records and compares them with DW-NOMINATE; relevant to the donors-and-primaries claim this paper leaves unevidenced.
A formal model (no data) of how presidential going-public can raise legislative polarization; a mechanism for the polarization trend this paper measures.

summary_issues: The Spearman agreements quoted (.960 House, .981 Senate) are pooled over 1789-1998, across party systems and the Civil Rights realignment; the summary should carry the UNSTRATIFIED label, as the analyst's own flag says.
The summary says party overlap is 'on dimension 1'; the text defines overlap as members closer to the opposing party's mean than their own and does not state the dimension.

The summary states DW-NOMINATE appears only via dw_control.py and Nokken-Poole scores; within fec, hearing_antagonism_build.py also imports dw_control, and paul_alignment's mention of behavior_panel.py and work_baseline.py as dw_control users was not confirmed by a search of fec.

'A read-only check confirms strong party sorting in several categories': the verifier re-ran the same function and reproduced it, but three categories (Mortgage & Housing, Fraud Prevention, Defense CU Issues) show no party split, and a same-function rerun is not an independent second path, so it remains UNVERIFIED (DE-062).
